question: A whole number larger than \(2\) leaves a remainder of \(2\) when divided by each of the numbers \(3,\) \(4,\) \(5,\) and \(6.\) The smallest such number lies between which two numbers?
solution:
Subtracting \(2\) removes the remainder in every division. Thus, if the desired number is \(n\), then \(n-2\) must be a common multiple of \(3,4,5,\) and \(6\). Since \(n>2\), this common multiple must be positive.

The positive common multiples of \(4\) and \(5\) begin \(20,40,60,\ldots\). Neither \(20\) nor \(40\) is divisible by \(6\), but \(60\) is. Also, every multiple of \(6\) is divisible by \(3\). Therefore \(60\) is the least positive common multiple of all four divisors.

Adding \(2\) gives \(n=62\). Because \(2\) is smaller than every listed divisor, this addition gives remainder \(2\) in each division. The smallest number is \(62\), which lies between \(60\) and \(79\), choice B.
